Start with the class or option type you need, then open a member to see its signature, arguments, defaults and return type. Use Find a member to narrow the list. Type names link to their own references, inherited members link to their base class, and Read implementation opens the checked-out source directly on this page.

The reference follows the TypeScript implementation, including constructor overloads and accessors. Where a live scene is available, run it beside the contract and use View source to experiment. The workflow links connect individual APIs to the guides that explain how to use them together.

Protected members support extensions; members marked internal expose engine machinery and are best understood alongside the rendering guides. Source comments and authored notes explain behavior where available. The collapsed declaration snapshot retains the earlier implementation inventory. See [current behavior and limitations](/limitations) for known differences between older comments and runtime behavior.

items: AlwaysOptions: Execution options for frame update callbacks registered with `always()`.
AlwaysContext: Rich contextual data and controls provided to the update callback.
AlwaysCallback: Callback function signature for `always()`. Return `false` to automatically stop and unregister the callback.
AlwaysHandle: Handle returned by `always()` to inspect and control the update task.
AlwaysTask: Internal representation of a registered update task.
AlwaysRegistry: Task registry for managing, sorting, and executing update tasks safely.

cells: Minimum interval between invocations in milliseconds (e.g. 100 = at most 10 times/second). The callback receives the accumulated `dt` elapsed since its last invocation. [Source line 11](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/Always.ts#L11).

Target frames per second (e.g. 12 = 12 updates per second). Automatically converted to `interval = 1000 / fps`. [Source line 17](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/Always.ts#L17).

Execution phase: - 'pre': Runs before scene animations and entity updates (default for Scene). - 'update': Runs during standard entity updates (default for Entity). - 'post': Runs after all entities and animations have updated. Essential for camera follow, look-at, and post-update constraints to avoid 1-frame jitter. [Source line 42](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/Always.ts#L42).
